nobox.final_span:
Growth; Representatives Sarah Bowman and Colleen Landrum; Representative Jess Ferguson; and Greenfield Mayor Roxanne Hemmingway Hathaway.
During the majority of the public session, commissioners concentrating on items related to COVID-19 relief funds.
A discussion on Highland County Jobs and Family Services' (JFS) request for Fiscal Year 2023 (FY23) Coronavirus Response Funds was brought forward. The FY23 allocation from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) was directed to the county’s JFS program in the amount of $1.823 million.
From that fund, commissioners approved $640,000 in a previous request and another $1,057,000 three weeks later.
Earlier in the session, Wilkin added the final $675,000 of the ARPA funds for commission review.
He explained that some of the remaining ARPA funds will be used for County Commissioners' Courts Discretionary needs.
Wilkin suggested that $175,000 of the remaining ARPA funds will be directed towards youth services at the Boys and Girls Club.
Wilkin said, “I cannot make a precedent with that $175 thou and all the different projects or I don’t even want to start wringing my hands right now because I don’t know what I think about all these things. But, I think it would be hard for me to defend a situation when I give the Boys and Girls Club funds, which were not requested by the Boys and Girls Clubs and we didn’t, I think it’d be very hard for me to defend, their increase in staff or the increase in their facilities or the increase in hours or the expansion when I don’t believe every JFS employee warrants that.”
